title: Improved $\ell_{p}$ Regression via Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares
claim: Our simple iterative method needs fewer iterations and less time than its direct predecessor, and it scales far better than generic solvers.
layout: 2x4 grid of line plots; top row iterations, bottom row time
description: A grid of line plots with eight panels labeled (a) to (h), though the right-hand panels (c), (d), (g) and (h) are cut off in this crop. The top row plots iteration counts and the bottom row plots wall-clock time. Panels (a) and (e) vary matrix size n at p=8. Panels (b) and (f) vary p from 3 to 10 at a fixed 500x400 size. Four colored curves with error bars appear in each: red for p-IRLS, blue for Ours, green for cvx SDPT3 and magenta for cvx sedumi. Blue stays below red in iterations and time. The CVX curves use fewer iterations but their time grows steeply, and they stop at n=1000. Legends sit in the top-left of each panel, and captions with the matrix sizes sit below the panels.
caption: \protectPerformance on random matrices: $\min\left\Vert Ax-b\right\Vert _{p}^{p}$ with $\epsilon=10^{-10}$. We compare our algorithm with CVX using SDPT3 and SeDuMi solvers and $p$-IRLS by [ref]. Figures (a),(b),(e),(f) plot the average and standard deviation of number of iterations and time taken by the solvers to find a solution over 10 runs. Figures (c),(d),(g),(h) measure over 5 runs.
abstract: We introduce fast algorithms for solving $\ell_{p}$ regression problems using the iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) method. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art iteration complexity, outperforming the IRLS algorithm by Adil-Peng-Sachdeva (NeurIPS 2019) and matching the theoretical bounds established by the complex algorithm of Adil-Kyng-Peng-Sachdeva (SODA 2019, J. ACM 2024) via a simpler lightweight iterative scheme. This bridges the existing gap between theoretical and practical algorithms for $\ell_{p}$ regression. Our algorithms depart from prior approaches, using a primal-dual framework, in which the update rule can be naturally derived from an invariant maintained for the dual objective. Empirically, we show that our algorithms significantly outperform both the IRLS algorithm by Adil-Peng-Sachdeva and MATLAB/CVX implementations.
